title: Moving in with grandparents; parents and coming to New York
summary: He moves with his mother to his paternal grandparents; describes the grandfather's origins, his mother's Barbarin family, and a note on arriving in New York at twenty.

blocks.x: And then what did you move to?

And I moved in the Southern Water, which is the French Quarter's part in the Southern Water section. And I moved in the Southern Water section. And I moved in the Bourbon and... Bourbon, which is called Fargo and Aron St. Claude with my mother.
They were raised in part of my grandparents.
My paternal grandparents were my father's mother. Ball.
Now where did you say he came from, Ball?

Ball came from Kentucky. Kentucky. It's a mystery to me how he came down south. He was going north. I think he was employed on one of the river boats. He settled in New Iberia. That's why I met my grandmother. He was born with four children. He moved in the Walther. And he worked as a stevedo, a long shaman on the river front. He read his children to tell the gun he came of age. He was not a twin, since my father met my mother. He was Rose Barbera. He was a daughter of Isidot Barbera.
